rendered: The premise does not hold: the document does not report that bare Al outperformed the carbon/Al current collector at 4 mA/cm^2[1]. It reports the opposite. Carbon/Al kept a low voltage hysteresis at high currents, with a 45 mV[2] hysteresis at 4 mA/cm^2[3]. By contrast, bare Al electrodes were prone to[4] failure at these currents[5]. So bare Al did not give a usable hysteresis at these currents, and the document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at that current, so no difference can be stated. The only comparison it makes is with previous work using Cu electrodes, which nearly double the hysteresis at[6] the same current. The document does not explain bare Al's failure beyond this, and it attributes the low hysteresis of carbon/Al to the carbon nucleation layer, which it probes with impedance spectroscopy.
